title: Everyday Chicken Curry
summary: A comforting, everyday chicken curry built on deeply browned onions and warm spices, simmered with tomatoes until the chicken is tender and the sauce is rich.
equipment: large heavy casserole or deep frying pan with lid (28 cm)

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
Kashmiri chilli powder or mild chilli powder
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Mix the chicken thigh pieces with the yoghurt, salt and turmeric in a bowl, and leave to marinate for at least 20 minutes, or up to overnight in the fridge. The yoghurt's mild acidity tenderises the meat gently while the turmeric starts colouring and flavouring it right through.

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large, heavy pan over medium heat and add the chopped onions with a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring regularly, for 15-18 minutes until deeply golden brown all over. This slow browning builds the sauce's depth of flavour, so resist rushing it on higher heat, which browns unevenly and can catch and burn.

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger and slit green chilli, and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant. These shorter-cooking aromatics would burn if added at the same time as the onions, so they go in once the onions are already soft and golden.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Add the cumin, coriander, chilli powder and 1 teaspoon of the garam masala with a small splash of water, and fry for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Blooming the spices in the hot oil and onion releases their aromatic oils, giving a rounder flavour than if they went straight into the watery sauce.

steps.title: Cook down the tomatoes
steps.text: Tip in the chopped tomatoes and salt, and cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until thickened, with a little oil visibly separating at the edges of the pan. That separation is a visual cue that the raw tomato taste has cooked away and the base is ready for the chicken.

steps.title: Simmer the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken, stirring to coat it in the sauce, and cook for 3 minutes. Pour in the water, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook gently for 20-25 minutes until the chicken is tender, the sauce has thickened, and the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) or above.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Stir in the remaining garam masala, the lemon juice and most of the chopped coriander, then let the curry rest off the heat for 5 minutes so the flavours settle. Scatter over the last of the coriander and serve with rice or flatbreads.

tips: Don't rush the onions - 15-18 minutes of steady, stirred cooking over medium heat builds the sauce's flavour; onions rushed on high heat burn in patches and turn bitter.
Wait until you see a little oil separating at the tomato stage before adding the chicken; it's the clearest sign the raw tomato taste has cooked out.
Use a thermometer to check the chicken has reached 74°C (165°F) rather than judging by time alone, since piece size can vary.
Marinating the chicken even briefly in yoghurt and turmeric makes a real difference to tenderness and colour, so don't skip it even when short on time.
storage: Cool and refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly in a pan or microwave, stirring occasionally, until piping hot and 74°C (165°F) throughout. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour on a day above 32°C (90°F)).
